newsitem.title: CANADA: United Grain Growers ruling due June 13.
newsitem.headline: United Grain Growers ruling due June 13.

text.p: A Manitoba judge will rule Friday on a lawsuit seeking to force United Grain Growers Ltd to hold a vote on its ability to issue new shares weeks before UGG planned to ask shareholders to approve a deal requiring three million new shares.
"The judge deferred the ruling to 10:30 (CDT/1130 EDT/1530 GMT) Friday morning," UGG lawyer Chris Martin told Reuters.

Oppenheimer & Co filed the lawsuit in Manitoba Court of Queen's Bench last week to force UGG to hold a vote June 26 on new share issuance and a poison pill instead of at a July 11 meeting on a deal with Archer Daniels Midland Co.
Oppenheimer owns 13.16 percent of UGG's outstanding limited common voting shares while a joint company of Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators owns 14.98 percent.
AWP and MPE scuttled a C$13.75 per share hostile take over bid for UGG in March after Manitoba Court of Queen's Bench ruled UGG's poison pill plan was legally valid.
UGG announced the tentative deal with ADM May 29 that would see C$113 million change hands and ADM acquire a 45 percent stake in the grain handler at C$16 a share.
UGG stocks traded up C$0.15 a share at C$15.35 at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT in thin volume of 6,082 shares.
